source: APLIIQ help center shipping rate sheet (US standard)
repricingNote: APLIIQ reprices when USPS does. Re-verify this table against the APLIIQ help center whenever USPS announces a rate change, then bump effectiveDate. Never edit a rate without moving the date with it.

billing.note: Freight is billed SEPARATELY from product cost. APLIIQ also charges a fulfillment fee PER PRODUCT (per unit), not per order.

domestic.lookupNote: Tier steps are IRREGULAR — never assume a uniform step and never interpolate. Select the first tier whose maxWeightOz is greater than or equal to the shipped weight. A weight above the last tier has no published rate and must be an explicit error, never a clamp to the last row.

international.dutiesNote: International stays DDU: the customer pays duties and import taxes on delivery. The storefront charges one flat international shipping fee per order (lib/commerce/policies.ts INTERNATIONAL_SHIPPING_CENTS).
international.source: APLIIQ rate sheet 2026-08-11_ShippingRates.csv (merchant-supplied), Standard service only. Upgraded and Rush columns exist in the source and are deliberately not modelled.
international.coverageNote: 208 destinations. Two deliberate omissions: tiers priced $0.00 in the sheet (24 rows) are DROPPED — a zero is APLIIQ signalling no service at that weight, not free shipping — and tiers above 640 oz are omitted as unreachable for apparel. Both cases make the lookup raise over_max_weight, which forces a manual quote instead of inventing a number.
international.serviceBreakNote: 26 destinations contain a tier where a HEAVIER parcel is cheaper, because a different carrier service takes over at the break (e.g. AT 70.4oz $74.84 then 80.0oz $56.05). This is real pricing, so the international parser sets allowServiceBreaks. Any worst-case estimate across a weight RANGE must take the max rate over the spanned tiers, never the rate at the heaviest point.
